title: Editing a custom `ArrayMesh` from the inspector steals mouse control and interrupts the edit
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.3.stable and 4.4.dev5

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev5 - Windows 10.0.22631 - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700F CPU @ 2.90GHz (16 threads)

### Issue description

When using the mouse to drag a value for a custom `ArrayMesh`, and the custom mesh's script uses  `ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays` to regenerate the mesh, it causes the mouse to lose grip of whatever control it was interacting with, and snap to the middle of the screen.

The use case here is implementing a custom, parametric mesh type. This bug makes it impossible to tweak the mesh with the mouse. You have to manually type in values.

Notes:
- This bug also happens if you use something like `MeshDataTools` or `SurfaceTool` to modify the mesh.
- This bug does _NOT_ happen if you use something like `ArrayMesh.surface_update_vertex_region`, but that does not perform all the necessary operations of generating a mesh (e.g. adding new vertices, triggering an AABB recalculation, etc.).
- UPDATE: This bug does _NOT_ happen if you use `RenderingServer.mesh_clear` and `RenderingServer.mesh_add_surface_from_arrays`.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bef0984-b262-4cd7-b260-020208a8c03b)


### Steps to reproduce

- Open the attached project/scene.
- Select the `triangle` node, and inspect its mesh, which has a `custom_mesh.gd` script attached.
- Use the mouse to edit its `Size` property.
- Observe that the value only changes by a small amount before the cursor is stolen away.
